html:
The Nomatsigenga are an Arawakan-speaking people of the central Peruvian Amazon, living in the Pangoa district of Junín, where the Andes drop into the forest. They are part of the Campa group of peoples, closely related to the larger Asháninka and to the Matsigenka further south.

They farm manioc and other crops in forest gardens, hunt and fish. Colonists and coffee farmers moved onto their land through the 1900s. In the 1980s and 1990s the Shining Path guerrillas held parts of the region and forced many Nomatsigenga and Asháninka into their camps, one of the darkest episodes of Peru's internal conflict. Their language belongs to the Arawakan family.
